tier_reason: Independent but small third-party suite (GeoToolbox, benchmark code public in the repo) compares directly against Boost.Geometry 1.90 R*-tree, with per-run numbers in linked TSVs; compiler named (MSVC 2026, clang-cl 22) but flags unstated and hardware given only as a laptop model (ASUS ROG Strix G16), no CPU model, so not A; not a well-known suite, so not B.

corrections.claimed_speedup: GeoToolbox README: tidwall R-tree is 'faster than Boost at insert/erase/reinsert and at querying afterwards'. Linked result TSVs (ikolev21.github.io, Insert-Erase-Query scenario, Boost time / tidwall time, geomean over 69 dataset/size/dim combinations): clang-cl insert 23.7x, erase 3.6x, reinsert 9.4x, range query 1.06x (range 0.30-2.54x), total 4.9x; MSVC insert 34.8x, erase 3.4x, reinsert 9.4x, query 1.08x, total 6.0x; at 10^6 elements total 10.9x (clang-cl) / 12.6x (MSVC) (derived from page data). Own README: 1M random points insert 151.3 ns/op, search-item 242.4 ns/op (clang-17 -O3, Ryzen 9 5950X), no Boost comparison.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: GeoToolbox: MSVC 2026 and clang-cl (Clang 22), x64, flags not stated; own README: clang-17 -O3
corrections.hardware: GeoToolbox: ASUS ROG Strix G16 laptop, Windows 11 (CPU model not stated); own README: AMD Ryzen 9 5950X, Ubuntu 20.04
corrections.caveats: Third-party comparison is a small, low-visibility repo; range-query speed vs Boost is roughly at parity (geomean ~1.06-1.08x, worst 0.3x), the large wins are in dynamic insert/erase/reinsert; tidwall is the heaviest index in memory; no bulk-loading, so order-sensitive. Ratios are derived from the linked TSVs, not stated on the README.

notes: Real win vs Boost R*-tree on dynamic updates (insert ~20-35x), query parity. Could rise to A if GeoToolbox's CMake flags and the laptop CPU model are pinned down.
